definitions.explanation: The formal ceremony held for a deceased person. In Japan, funerals typically follow Buddhist traditions, though Shinto and Christian services also occur.

examples.japanese: {葬儀|そうぎ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{明日|あした}→明日：00501_ashita⟧⟦{行|おこな}われる→行う：01238_okonau⟧。
examples.english: The funeral will be held tomorrow.

examples.japanese: {葬儀|そうぎ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{参列|さんれつ}→参列：11888_sanretsu⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧⟦ため→ため：01145_tame⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{黒|くろ}い→黒い：00588_kuroi⟧⟦{服|ふく}→服：00695_fuku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{着|き}た→着る：00541_kiru⟧。
examples.english: I wore black clothes to attend the funeral.

examples.japanese: {葬儀|そうぎ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{準備|じゅんび}→準備：01431_junbi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{葬儀社|そうぎしゃ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{任|まか}せる→任せる：02417_makaseru⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧。
examples.english: Funeral preparations are often left to the funeral home.

notes:
USAGE:
The standard formal word for a funeral ceremony. In Japan, funerals often consist of two parts: ⟦{通夜|つや}→通夜：16026_tsuya⟧ (wake, held the evening before) and {葬儀|そうぎ}/⟦{告別式|こくべつしき}→告別式：05923_kokubetsushiki⟧ (funeral/farewell ceremony).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {葬儀|そうぎ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{行|おこな}う→行う：01238_okonau⟧ (to hold a funeral)
- {葬儀|そうぎ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{参列|さんれつ}→参列：11888_sanretsu⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (to attend a funeral)
- {葬儀社|そうぎしゃ} (funeral home, funeral director)
- ⟦{葬儀場|そうぎじょう}→葬儀場：25807_sougijou⟧ (funeral hall)
- {家族葬|かぞくそう} (family-only funeral)
